question: Does a narrow second sweep of an equal 15m swing with regular RSI divergence, followed by a range-regime neckline break and retest, have positive expectancy after stress costs?
mechanism: The second top/bottom takes resting liquidity but fails to gain momentum. A confirmed return inside the level plus RSI non-confirmation identifies the trap; the neckline break confirms a structure change and its retest supplies the entry.
difference_from_rejected_S112_S114: No order block, FVG or counter-trend 1h context. H3 requires two comparable confirmed extremes, a controlled 0.03-0.35 ATR sweep, regular RSI divergence, low-ADX 1h/4h range context and a neckline retest. Target is 1.5R intraday rather than 3R over 72h.

setup.pivots: confirmed 15m width-2 swings separated by 6-32 bars
setup.sweep: second extreme exceeds the first by 0.03-0.35 ATR and its candle closes back inside
setup.divergence: regular RSI divergence >=3 points; first bottom RSI <=35 or first top RSI >=65
setup.mss: within four 15m bars after the second pivot is known, directional close breaks the intervening neckline by 0.03 ATR
setup.entry: 30-minute post-only limit retest at the neckline
setup.stop: beyond the second sweep extreme plus 0.15 ATR; distance 0.60%-1.25%
setup.session: MSS from 06:00 inclusive to 18:00 exclusive UTC

gates.development_stress: at least 40 fills, net PnL > 0, PF >1.10 and mean net R >0
gates.validation_stress: at least 20 fills, net PnL >=0, PF >=1.00, at least three positive symbols, largest symbol <=50% of gross profit

no_parameter_search: Exactly one configuration; failure closes this H3 version.
